title: A steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based BCI dataset in children and adolescents
description: EEG recordings from 47 neurotypical children and adolescents (5-18 years) who each completed a two-stage SSVEP-based brain-computer interface session. The first stage was a stimulus personalization pipeline. The second was an online 4-target SSVEP game. Data were recorded with a 16-channel g.tec gel-based system at 256 Hz and released to support signal-processing methods developed specifically for pediatric SSVEP-BCI data.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.tec g.GAMMAsys gel-based system (g.USBamp, g.GAMMAcap) using 16 channels at 256 Hz, an earlobe reference and an Fpz ground. Participants completed a stimulus personalization task with 12 stimuli (4 contrasts x 3 sizes) flickering at 10 Hz, followed by an online 4-target SSVEP game at 6.25, 10, 11.11 and 14.28 Hz. The game used a personal stimulus and a high-contrast standard stimulus on two themed maps. Original XDF recordings were converted to BIDS BrainVision files with mne-bids.
